name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body: There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign: Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: In the dead of winter, as frigid winds howled through the jagged peaks of the Wyrmwall Mountains, a relentless pursuit unfolded. Barbaric invaders from a distant continent bore down on a ragtag band of human defenders, who fled deeper into the inhospitable heights, the white shroud of snow concealing their desperate retreat. Amidst the relentless chase, a cloaked observer watched from a rocky crag high above the battlefield, a figure concealed in shadows, long estranged from humanity and their endless wars. The invaders, with their monstrous war machines belching smoke and fire, marched with an otherworldly ferocity, gears and pistons clanking in discordant harmony, as they advanced relentlessly into the mountains. The defenders fought back with crackling arcs of lightning and thunderous firearms. But they were outmatched, desperately fighting for their lives as they fled across the unforgiving landscape. "Tsk, tsk," the watcher whispered, "the more things change, the more they stay the same. Isn’t that right, Hushwig?"

name: Name
body: With a skeletal finger, he scratched at the nape of an enormous white hare crouched beside him. Zacchaeus, once known as the Winter’s Chill for the famine and strife that followed in his wake, had been wandering the fringes of humanity after escaping the captivity of a wicked crone. Free for the first time in ages, he was searching for a new purpose, but he had little hope of finding it among these warring factions. Yet he watched with a morbid curiosity, for the brutal clash developing below his perch was a testament to the Iron Kingdoms’ indomitable spirit, even in the face of impending doom. The giant hare suddenly stood bolt upright, ears twitching as one massive back paw thumped thrice on the ground. Something beyond the raging battle had spooked him, a disturbance in the ancient heart of the mountains that echoed through the frozen night. Zacchaeus could sense a presence awakening, a primeval force long dormant stirring in the depths. What role this force would play intrigued the elder grymkin, as it cast an eerie uncertainty over the outcome of the savage conflict.

name: Name
body: As the invaders and defenders continued to clash on the unforgiving slopes, Zacchaeus knew the destiny of the Iron Kingdoms hung in the balance, and the emergence of this enigmatic entity from the depths of the mountains would alter the fate of both sides indelibly. "There now, Hushwig," Zacchaeus said, stroking the rabbit’s thick fur to calm him. "Let us see how this plays out." Black Tide Season 3, Chapter 3 is made up of three scenarios that should be played in order: "The High Ground," "A Difficult Crossing," and "Firebreather."

name: Name
body: In the heart of winter’s icy grip, defenders of their homeland race against time, their breath forming frosty clouds in the frigid air. High amidst the treacherous mountain terrain, they rally to fortify a crucial passage of a winding, ancient road. A merciless horde descends upon them, a relentless force with eyes fixed on their prize. But at stake are the defenders’ coveted territories and their vulnerable people. Failure is not an option. With every swing of hammer and clash of steel, the defenders fight for survival, a grim and vital line between a future of order or chaos.

name: Name
body:
The Defenders rush to fortify a vital pass along an ancient road high in the mountains against an Invader assault. Should the Invaders seize the pass, they will have disrupted the Defender’s supply lines and gain unfettered access to the territories beyond. Failure will force them to find longer and more dangerous pathways into the mountains.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender builds a 50-point army..
The Invader builds a 75-point army.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, the Invader deploys to an area 10" forward of the north table edge.
The Defender deploys to an area 7" forward of the south table edge. In front of the Defender’s Deployment Zone is a 10" x 48"  area of impassable terrain that is only divided by the 10" x 10" Pass Zone. Sitting directly to the left of the Pass Zone abutting the impassable terrain is a Guard Tower terrain feature.
Players then take turns each placing four hills anywhere on the table outside the impassable terrain and the Deployment Zones.
Players then take turns each placing four additional terrain features. These terrain features can be placed on hills, but cannot be placed within 4" of the impassable terrain, either player’s Deployment Zone, or another non-hill terrain feature.
Neither player can place defenses when playing this scenario.
The Defender deploys first and can deploy models/units into the Guard Tower.
The Invader takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Starting with the Defender’s second turn, a player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for securing either the Guard Tower or the Pass Zone.
If the Guard Tower is destroyed, the Invader scores 3 Victory Points.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If the Guard Tower has not been destroyed after six rounds, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest Points. If the Invader destroys the Guard Tower and secures the Pass Zone in the same turn, the Invader wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 Victory Points or more than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body:
With every step, the invaders closed the distance, their hunger for victory mirrored only by the defenders' determination to protect their lands. A river, its icy currents swift and merciless, emerged as their final line of defense. The defenders exchanged solemn glances, weighing their few and terrible options, understanding the grim reality that now unfolded before them.
Their bridges, once their lifeline to escape, could now become the instruments of their salvation or their doom. Destruction was the only path left to them. Yet the thought of severing the links to the world they knew, the world that cradled their homes and lives, filled them with a profound sorrow and an unshakable dread. But only through sacrifice would any survive.

name: Name
body:
As the action moves into the mountains, the Invaders must perform a dangerous crossing over a fast-moving river in the highlands. Meanwhile, the desperate defenders are forced to contemplate the unthinkable to slow the Invader’s advance: destroying their own bridges to buy much needed time.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, a 4" wide river runs through the middle of the battlefield along the Invader’s side of the table. The river is difficult terrain.
Three 6" x 8" bridges span the river, one 6" from each of the east and west sides of the table and one across the center of the river. Bridges are considered to be buildings with DEF 5, ARM 18, and 20 damage boxes. Any models on a bridge when it is destroyed are removed from play.
Players then alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to four features. A player cannot place terrain within 4" of a Deployment Zone, table edge, the river, or another terrain feature.
The Invader cannot place defenses in this scenario.
The Invader deploys their models first and takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
A player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each bridge they are securing.
The Invader player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of their turn if they have one or more models completely on the Defender’s side of the river at the start of their turn.
Each time a bridge is destroyed, the Defender receives 1 Victory Point.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If the Invader holds all three bridges at the beginning of any of their turns, they win the match and gain 5 War Chest Points. If at any time all three bridges are destroyed and the Invader has no models on the Defender’s side of the river, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Trapped in their encampment on the precipice of an abandoned powder mine, the defenders dance with the invaders on the edge of oblivion. The crimson earth beneath them lays bare a volatile truth: the red powder, highly explosive, awaits a single spark to engulf them all. Both sides maneuver with deadly caution, fear of igniting an inferno under their feet lurking in every mind. The battlefield is a powder keg, and the choreography of their movements provides a perilous overture to the cataclysmic battle that looms.

name: Name
body:
The Invaders have finally cornered the Defenders at their mountain camp located at the site of an old abandoned red powder mine. As the battle erupts, both sides must carefully consider the implications of the residual powder deposits as they work to achieve their strategic goals without blowing the mountain apart at its seams.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, a 5" x 5" Mine Entrance objective sits in the middle of the table on the west side of the battlefield. The Mine Entrance objective is an obstruction.
Four 3" x 5" trenches are positioned on the east side of the battlefield in pairs with a gap of 4" between them.
The Defender then places three 3" x 5" Command Tent objectives anywhere on their side of the table. Command Tent objectives cannot be placed within 3" of the Defender’s Deployment Zone, another Command Tent, or a table edge. Command Tent objectives are obstructions.
Players then take turns each placing three Powder Keg Defenses anywhere within 12" of the Mine Entrance.
Players then take turns each placing two additional terrain features. A player cannot place terrain within 4" of a Deployment Zone, table edge, trench, Mine Entrance, Command Tent, table edge, or another terrain feature.
The Invader cannot place additional defenses in this scenario.
The winner of "The High Ground" scenario decides which player deploys first.

name: Name
body: The winner of the "Difficult Crossing" scenario decides which player takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Tinderbox: The entire area surrounding the mine is coated with a fine layer of red blasting powder. The residual deposits of powder only get heavier the closer they get to the Mine Entrance. Each time a model makes a ranged or arcane attack that causes fire damage, immediately after the attack is resolved, roll a d6. On a roll of 2, the attacking model suffers the fire continuous effect. On a roll of 1, the blasting powder explodes, causing the attacking model and any models within 2" of it to each suffer a POW 10 blast damage roll. On any other roll, nothing happens.
Gobber Spy Mission: Players who include Reinholdt, Gobber Spy in their force can undertake the following covert missions:
Defender: Rear Guard—Reinholdt, Gobber Spy can make a Rear Guard special action once per game while in the Invader’s Deployment Zone. When he does so, the Defender gains 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.
Invader: Gather Intel—Reinholdt, Gobber Spy can make the Gather Intel special action once per game while in base contact with a Command Tent objective. When he does so, the Invader gains 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body:
The Defender scores 2 Victory Points at the start of each of their turns if they are securing the Mine Entrance objective.
The Invader scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each Command Tent objective they are securing.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: At the beginning of any of their turns beginning with the third, if a player is securing all three Command Tent objectives and the Mine Entrance objective, they win the match and receive 6 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
